raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

GLM-5.3-Flash fails after load when the KV dtype, DSA backend and GPU cannot read pooled rows (`index_kpool > 1`). Users report it with FP8 KV on H20 (#36830), and on SM120 with default backends and BF16 KV (#37105) or with explicit backends (#39302). On one B200 with a reduced config and dummy weights, main exits after 36 to 45 s and this PR after 12 to 18 s. Real weights were not measured.

This PR rejects these configurations at startup and lists the allowed backends. Rejected pairs still do not serve.

#47237 refuses `trtllm` outside SM100, SM103 and SM107, which catches the SM120 defaults but not `flashmla_kv`, `fa3` or `flashmla_sparse`.

## Modifications

Startup and the runtime guard share one capability table. A PD node checks only its starting role.

This PR also corrects the cookbook note on FP8 KV with TileLang DSA, because the new error lists that pair.

Recipes (TPU7x not traced) and ROCm startup do not change.

Startup skips learnable-sink, SM12x FP8 `GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM` and HiSparse. A prefill node with an unsupported decode backend, and SM102 with `trtllm` (by code reading), pass startup and can fail after load.

Whichever merges later adapts: #38430 or #45298 (SM12x backend), #44217 (SM90 Q8 prefill, cookbook sentence), #47237 (table rows).

## Accuracy Tests

No accuracy eval ran on this branch.

| KV dtype, prefill, decode | main exit | This PR exit | Commits |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| FP8, `flashmla_kv`, `flashmla_kv` | 45 s with `--disable-flashinfer-autotune`, `index_kpool > 1 appends tail tokens to topk_indices and is currently only supported by the FA3/TileLang/TRTLLM DSA prefill backend.` Default flags say `DSA decode backend`. | 18 s, new `ValueError` | `d3f12b9169`, main `2dc5bdd18b` |
| FP8, `fa3`, `fa3` | 45 s, `flash_attn at sgl-kernel is only supported on sm90 and above` | 15 s, new `ValueError` | `d3f12b9169`, main `2dc5bdd18b` |
| FP8, `flashmla_sparse`, `flashmla_sparse` | 45 s, `Expected head dim 512 for query and kv_cache, got 512 and 528` | 12 s, new `ValueError` | `d3f12b9169`, main `2dc5bdd18b` |
| BF16, `fa3`, `fa3` | 45 s, `flash_attn at sgl-kernel is only supported on sm90 and above` | 12 s, new `ValueError` | `d3f12b9169`, main `2dc5bdd18b` |
| BF16, `flashmla_sparse_q8`, `tilelang` | 36 s, `flashmla_sparse_q8 is SM90-only` | 12 s, new `ValueError` | `d3f12b9169`, main `2dc5bdd18b` |
| FP8, `flashmla_sparse`, `trtllm`, prefill node | 39 to 44 s, `Expected head dim 512 for query and kv_cache, got 512 and 528` | 12 to 13 s, new `ValueError` | Autotune on: main `ba1ed00dfe` and `cbfc0932e3`, and this branch merged with each |
| FP8, `trtllm`, `flashmla_sparse`, decode node | 38 to 44 s, `Expected head dim 512 for query and kv_cache, got 512 and 528` | 12 to 14 s, new `ValueError` | Autotune on: main `ba1ed00dfe` and `cbfc0932e3`, and this branch merged with each |

Working pairs serve on both trees. The table test fails on main for rejected rows.

Override and k-pool tests pass on `e599e15d71` merged with main `ba1ed00dfe`, except where main also fails. Later commits change only a comment, an import and the cookbook sentence.

The cookbook sentence rests on real FP8 weights and FP8 KV on 4x B200 with sgl-eval 0.1.3 GSM8K. TileLang at `ba1ed00dfe` scored 81.50% with 16.5% of answers ending in a run of `!`, and TRT-LLM at `582168dd7c` scored 98.00% with none. On dummy weights at 33 and 41 concurrent requests, the #47013 kernel removed that output.

```bash
# The TRT-LLM run differs from the cookbook's B200 Low Latency flags by --tp-size 4 (cookbook: 8), --trust-remote-code and --served-model-name glm.
# This TileLang run differs from that TRT-LLM run only in the two DSA backends, the port and the random seed.
python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path <GLM-5.3-Flash FP8 weights> --served-model-name glm \
  --trust-remote-code --host 127.0.0.1 --port <port> \
  --tp-size 4 \
  --dsa-prefill-backend tilelang --dsa-decode-backend tilelang --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \
  --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_trtllm \
  --speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-num-steps 5 \
  --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 6 \
  --reasoning-parser auto --tool-call-parser auto
sgl-eval run gsm8k --base-url http://127.0.0.1:<port>/v1 --model glm --num-examples 200 --num-threads 64 \
  --max-tokens 32768 --temperature 1.0 --top-p 0.95 --thinking
```

Not verified: Hopper or SM120 GPUs, real weights on this branch or with #47013, PD KV transfer, `--enable-pd-role-switch`, docs build, and CI test workflows.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

files.patch:
@@ -185,7 +185,7 @@ Keep the checkpoint's KDA lower-bound setting unchanged. In particular, do not o
 
 ### Keep the KV and DSA backends paired
 
-On Blackwell, the recipes default to an FP8 KV cache with TRT-LLM DSA: on GB300 this pairing measured 2.9–5.7% higher throughput and about 1.8x the KV token capacity at identical pool bytes, with GSM8K accuracy within noise of BF16. BF16 KV with TileLang DSA remains selectable in the deployment panel and is the default on H100 and H200, where FP8 KV with TRT-LLM DSA is disabled. MI355X instead uses FP8 KV with TileLang DSA in the recorded ROCm recipe. Switch the dtype and both DSA backends together; TileLang DSA with FP8 KV is not a valid CUDA combination, and TRT-LLM DSA is not the MI355X backend.
+On Blackwell, the recipes default to an FP8 KV cache with TRT-LLM DSA: on GB300 this pairing measured 2.9–5.7% higher throughput and about 1.8x the KV token capacity at identical pool bytes, with GSM8K accuracy within noise of BF16. BF16 KV with TileLang DSA remains selectable in the deployment panel and is the default on H100 and H200, where FP8 KV with TRT-LLM DSA is disabled. MI355X instead uses FP8 KV with TileLang DSA in the recorded ROCm recipe. Switch the dtype and both DSA backends together; TRT-LLM DSA is not the MI355X backend. On CUDA, the server accepts TileLang DSA with FP8 KV when both backends are `tilelang`, but this pairing is not qualified for this model: builds without [PR #47013](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/47013) can return a run of `!` for short prompts under concurrent requests.
 
 On Hopper, BF16 KV can also run the sparse prefill in FP8 with `--dsa-prefill-backend flashmla_sparse_q8` (decode stays on `tilelang` and the cache stays BF16): on H200 this pairing measured 5.8–12.1% higher throughput on prefill-only requests, with GSM8K accuracy within noise of BF16 + TileLang. It is SM90-only and requires a build that includes [PR #41790](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/41790); FP8 KV is not available with it for this model.

@@ -590,6 +590,72 @@ def _check_dsa_backend_constraints(
         raise ValueError("CUDA TileLang FP8 KV requires SM89 or newer.")
 
 
+def _check_dsa_kpool_backend_support(
+    hf_config: Any,
+    kv_cache_dtype: str,
+    prefill_backend: Optional[str],
+    decode_backend: Optional[str],
+    *,
+    device_sm_major: int,
+    disaggregation_mode: str,
+) -> None:
+    """Reject DSA backends that cannot serve an index_kpool > 1 model.
+
+    Without this check the server loads the weights and then fails in CUDA
+    graph capture with NotImplementedError from _check_kpool_tail_backend.
+    """
+    from sglang.srt.configs.model_config import get_dsa_index_kpool
+    from sglang.srt.layers.attention.dsa.kpool_backend import (
+        kpool_tail_backends,
+        resolve_kpool_tail_backend,
+    )
+
+    index_kpool = get_dsa_index_kpool(hf_config)
+    if index_kpool <= 1:
+        return
+    # A PD node serves only its own role, and calculate_mla_kv_cache_dim reads only
+    # that role. A literal trtllm there keeps FP8 rows raw. FlashInfer autotune on a
+    # prefill node also runs a decode dummy, so an unsupported decode backend still
+    # fails after load in _check_kpool_tail_backend.
+    roles = {"prefill": prefill_backend, "decode": decode_backend}
+    if disaggregation_mode in roles:
+        roles = {disaggregation_mode: roles[disaggregation_mode]}
+    bf16_kv = kv_cache_dtype == "bfloat16"
+    packed_fp8 = not bf16_kv and "trtllm" not in roles.values()
+    sparse_target = resolve_kpool_tail_backend(
+        "flashmla_sparse", device_sm_major, packed_fp8=not bf16_kv
+    )
+    supported = []
+    unsupported = []
+    for phase, backend in roles.items():
+        backends = kpool_tail_backends(
+            phase, bf16_kv=bf16_kv, device_sm_major=device_sm_major
+        )
+        names = (
+            (*backends, "flashmla_sparse") if sparse_target in backends else backends
+        )
+        supported.append(f"Supported {phase} backends: {', '.join(names)}.")
+        # set_dsa_prefill_impl picks flashmla_sparse for auto over unpacked rows.
+        # Packed rows reject either name.
+        chosen = backend
+        if phase == "prefill" and backend == "flashmla_auto":
+            chosen = "flashmla_sparse"
+        chosen = resolve_kpool_tail_backend(
+            chosen, device_sm_major, packed_fp8=packed_fp8
+        )
+        if chosen not in backends:
+            unsupported.append(f"{phase}={backend}")
+    if not unsupported:
+        return
+    raise ValueError(
+        f"{hf_config.architectures[0]} sets index_kpool={index_kpool}, and the "
+        f"{', '.join(unsupported)} DSA backend does not support index_kpool > 1 "
+        f"(kv_cache_dtype={kv_cache_dtype}, prefill={prefill_backend}, "
+        f"decode={decode_backend}, sm_major={device_sm_major}). "
+        f"{' '.join(supported)}"
+    )
+
+
 def _check_tilelang_dsa_fp8_kv(
     kv_cache_dtype: str,
     prefill_backend: Optional[str],
@@ -741,6 +807,15 @@ def _dsa_split_backend_resolution(view: Any) -> dict:
         hip=get_platform().is_hip,
         dcp_size=getattr(view, "dcp_size", 1) or 1,
     )
+    if not get_platform().is_hip:
+        _check_dsa_kpool_backend_support(
+            hf_config,
+            kv_cache_dtype,
+            prefill,
+            decode,
+            device_sm_major=major,
+            disaggregation_mode=getattr(view, "disaggregation_mode", "null"),
+        )
     logger.warning(
         f"Set DSA backends for {kv_cache_dtype} KV Cache: "
         f"prefill={prefill}, decode={decode}."

@@ -5,6 +5,10 @@
 
 import torch
 
+from sglang.srt.layers.attention.dsa.kpool_backend import (
+    kpool_tail_backends,
+    resolve_kpool_tail_backend,
+)
 from sglang.srt.layers.attention.dsa.kpool_plan import (
     init_kpool_extend_metadata,
     init_kpool_write_plan,
@@ -39,43 +43,33 @@ def _check_kpool_tail_backend(
         dsa_impl: _DSA_IMPL_T,
         phase: str,
     ) -> None:
-        # q8 prefill consumes the tail columns as ragged ids, like the history
-        # picks. Only over a bfloat16 pool: gathering packed fp8 rows through
-        # kpool tail columns is untested, so that combination keeps the guard.
-        if (
-            dsa_impl == "flashmla_sparse_q8"
-            and phase == "prefill"

+"""Backend capabilities for pooled DSA tail tokens."""
+
+
+def kpool_tail_backends(
+    phase: str, *, bf16_kv: bool, device_sm_major: int
+) -> tuple[str, ...]:
+    """Return the backends that read a pooled tail on this KV dtype and GPU.
+
+    FA3 needs BF16 rows and does not run on Blackwell. Q8 prefill reads the tail
+    columns as ragged ids and runs only on SM90. Packed FP8 rows through those
+    columns are untested. FlashInfer's trtllm-gen MLA runs only on SM10x.
+    """
+    if device_sm_major == 10:
+        return ("tilelang", "trtllm")
+    if not bf16_kv or device_sm_major > 10:
+        return ("tilelang",)
+    if phase == "prefill" and device_sm_major == 9:
+        return ("tilelang", "fa3", "flashmla_sparse_q8")
+    return ("tilelang", "fa3")
+
+
+def resolve_kpool_tail_backend(
+    backend: str, device_sm_major: int, *, packed_fp8: bool
+) -> str:
+    """Map flashmla_sparse to the kernel that reads the pooled tail tokens.
+
+    Neither target reads packed FP8 rows, so the name stays as it is there.
+    """
+    if backend != "flashmla_sparse" or packed_fp8:
+        return backend
+    if device_sm_major >= 10:
+        return "trtllm"
+    if device_sm_major == 9:
+        return "fa3"
+    return backend

Ready for review at dcb2b5abbc. The branch is rebased onto the required current-main base, with a verified signed commit. The focused resolver regression fails on the base with `ValueError not raised` and passes on this branch; scoped pre-commit also passes. This is CPU validation with mocked Hopper properties, not a new Hopper server run. Could a maintainer enable `run-ci`?
@Fridge003, could you review the pooled DSA backend validation? It reports unsupported configurations during argument resolution, before loading the model.

This interacts with #38430, which adds `flashinfer_sparse_mla` (FlashInfer's native sparse MLA path for GLM-5.3-Flash on SM120) to `_check_kpool_tail_backend`; that backend handles the pooled tail tokens. With the allowlist here, an explicit `--dsa-prefill-backend` / `--dsa-decode-backend flashinfer_sparse_mla` would be rejected at startup even after #38430 merges, so `_DSA_KPOOL_TAIL_BACKENDS` needs `flashinfer_sparse_mla` whichever PR lands first.

Building the allowlist and the error text from the set `_check_kpool_tail_backend` accepts, plus the remapped `flashmla_sparse`, would keep them aligned; the "Supported backends: fa3, tilelang, trtllm" text already omits `flashmla_sparse`.

Startup and runtime now share the capability definition in `kpool_backend.py`, including the FlashMLA remap and phase/dtype rules. The error text comes from those capabilities, and BF16 Q8 prefill stays valid. I checked the combination with #38430: its native implementation needs to add `flashinfer_sparse_mla` to `KPOOL_TAIL_BACKENDS` and retain the shared guard during merge resolution. The affected CPU backend checks pass with that addition. Current main still rejects the unsupported route until the native implementation lands.
